concrete_path: An untrusted child replaces /work/stderr.log with a symlink or other non-regular entry, stops its supervisor, and remains alive until the fixed outer watchdog fires.
The supervisor cannot produce its post-reap report; the resource file is still empty or otherwise unauthoritative.
The host kills/reaps the outer process, then the stderr metadata branch returns process_valid=false before checking outer_timed_out and not accounted.
The evaluator treats a returned invalid process as a failed scientific stage instead of aborting as infrastructure_error with score=null.
findings.follow_up_fixture: Mock an expired outer watchdog with no accounting and symlink/non-regular/missing stderr; each must abort with infrastructure_error and null score. Test an ordinary genuine worker timeout separately: that remains a resource failure.
findings.impact: Violates the promised no-authoritative-accounting timeout classification. Does not make process_valid true, extend the worker budget, or create a passing score.
findings.issue: The non-regular/non-single-link stderr early return precedes the outer_timed_out and not accounted infrastructure exception. Missing stderr also raises before the intended infrastructure classification.
findings.minimal_recommendation: Move the existing outer_timed_out and not accounted SandboxUnavailable check immediately after accounting parsing and before stderr metadata/read/early-return handling. Keep the pass gate unchanged.
findings.runtime_reproduction: Not executed; this is a static control-flow counterexample, not a reproduced grade or sandbox escape.
findings.severity: medium: result classification, not false acceptance

example.accounting: protected supervisor wait4 on direct solver child

findings.impact: The example passes the resource parser when the outer exit is zero. No child-to-success exploit is established: on that path the protected supervisor has already reaped the only untrusted child and rewritten the report with genuine numeric/integer fields. This is not a false-pass blocker under that trust boundary.
findings.issue: CPU and wall are float-coerced, and isinstance(child_exitcode, int) accepts JSON booleans. The parser is finite/bounded but not a strict numeric/integer schema; default json.loads also does not reject duplicate keys.
findings.minimal_recommendation: If strict malformed-report rejection is required, check exact integer/non-bool numeric types before conversion and reject duplicate keys. Do not replace or weaken the protected final-write/clean-exit requirement.
findings.runtime_reproduction: Not executed; parser behavior is derived directly from the expressions.

changes: Check outer timeout without authoritative accounting before any stderr access or early return (WG-01).
Read supervisor bootstrap from the same staged worker copy used by the solver child.
focused_tests: Outer timeout plus no accounting with missing, symlink or nonregular stderr must abort as null-score infrastructure.
An authenticated worker wall timeout remains a resource failure, not an infrastructure waiver.
Live source mutation after staging cannot change either staged worker execution path.

nonblocking_caveats.assessment: Post-SIGKILL reaps remain blocking; host Popen construction and filesystem cleanup are also outside a separately bounded cleanup loop. Thus 120+wall is the polling trigger, not a demonstrated absolute end-to-end return cap under uninterruptible kernel/IO stalls. This can hang/invalidate but is not a false-pass path.
nonblocking_caveats.recommendation: Retain an outer harness operational deadline and verify no live namespace after timeout. Do not infer a solver result if cleanup/accounting is incomplete. A stronger cleanup guarantee needs separate containment, not a timer reset.

nonblocking_caveats.assessment: The child worker is staged once but supervisor bootstrap is read again from the live source. Concurrent source edits can mix worker revisions. This is a deployment/coherence risk, not a submitted-child escape.
nonblocking_caveats.recommendation: Keep graders quiescent across paired deployment; optionally read the supervisor bootstrap from the same staged worker copy. Record source hashes for already-running tests.

tampering_review.assessment: Edits after solver launch cannot change the supervisor local wall_limit or host request object; child resource setup occurs before submitted code.

The file is same-UID writable while the child runs; its existence and early contents are not authentication. In the successful path, reap precedes identity checking and the last trusted rewrite, so no untrusted descendant may remain to race it.
Missing or changed inode/link identity invalidates the supervisor. Restoring the original inode before child exit still leaves the trusted final rewrite. No timer depends on this marker.

Stopping/signaling the supervisor can cause delay, invalidation or the outer guard. It cannot reset the monotonic start or grant a clean authenticated pass. WG-01 concerns the resulting failure classification only.
The existing nondumpable/capability/seccomp/close-fds barriers are unchanged. This review found no new bypass in the patch, but did not empirically probe those barriers.

Normal report emission follows direct-child reap. That rules out the direct child remaining alive; absence of additional untrusted processes relies on the unchanged seccomp barrier. Host-kill namespace cleanup still merits the existing regression probe.

verdict: No concrete false-pass or timer-reset escape found in the reviewed patch. One confirmed timeout-classification ordering gap (WG-01); defensive schema and operational/deployment caveats remain. This is not empirical sandbox certification.

verified_static_invariants.result: Supervisor reads wall before spawn, takes one monotonic start before Popen, never rereads the request or resets the deadline.
One direct-PID wait4 owner polls WNOHANG, latches timeout, kills that PID, and reaps before final accounting. Elapsed wall is sampled immediately after the wait loop.
Actual elapsed wall is reported even if the wait4 completion branch wins a deadline race; the host still rejects a reported over-budget wall when worker_timed_out is false.
Nondumpable supervisor, exclusive/no-follow preopened report descriptor, post-reap inode/link check, close_fds=True, and final descriptor truncate/rewrite are preserved.
Existing pre-submission no-process/no-thread/no-exec and memory/FD/namespace syscall restrictions remain unchanged. Direct-child sufficiency depends on those restrictions actually holding.
Host watchdog is a fixed 120 seconds plus original wall budget, with no marker or timer resets. Outer elapsed time remains diagnostic instead of being substituted for the successful child wall.
Host checks finite nonnegative CPU/wall, boolean timeout, integer exit status and supervisor/outer exit consistency. Clean outer exit plus the mapping implies child exit zero on any passing path.
Pass additionally requires no timeout, valid accounting, and original host CPU/wall budgets. Missing/partial accounting cannot pass and outer CPU is not a passing fallback.
